title: Angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal
summary: Use corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle relationships.
objectives: Recognise corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle relationships.
Calculate unknown angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal.
Use angle relationships to justify when two lines are parallel.

sections.title: Recognising the F, Z and C relationships

blocks.text: For parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal, alternate interior angles are equal, and co-interior angles on the same side of a transversal total 180°.

A transversal crossing parallel lines creates matching angle positions. Corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, and co-interior angles on the same side total 180°. The arrow markings on the lines, rather than their appearance, establish that the lines are parallel.

Trace a Z shape for alternate angles, an F shape for corresponding angles and a C shape for co-interior angles, but always confirm which lines form the angle. Converse facts also work: if a valid pair of corresponding or alternate angles is equal, or co-interior angles total 180°, the lines are parallel.

blocks.text: Do not use a parallel-line fact unless parallel arrows are shown or parallelism has been proved. Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles are supplementary. Keep the transversal fixed when identifying the pair.

prompt.text: A corresponding angle is 68°. Find its matching angle.

feedback.text: Corresponding angles are equal when the lines are parallel.
